supersedesNote: Second addendum to _inbox/2026-09-07_ctx-f_close.json, following up the first addendum (2026-09-07T22-15-00Z). Resolves the reconciliation that addendum opened, and resolves doc-repo-26's own FACTORY_DATABASE_URL/FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO question. Does NOT change the merged gate code (PR #100, commit 570fb4c) -- per doc-repo-26's explicit, repeated instruction not to rebuild the instantiation check again this session without clear settled ground, this addendum records the reconciliation and specifies the correct next build rather than shipping a fourth iteration of the formula under time pressure.

reconciliationResolved.storeIdentity: FACTORY_DATABASE_URL and FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO are the SAME physical database (ep-round-base-au0jofwp.c-10.us-east-1.aws.neon.tech, db neondb) -- not different branches, not a hazard. Verified directly: FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO connects as role parcel_record_ro, which lacks a grant on landing_cad_property entirely (confirmed: `SELECT ... FROM landing_cad_property` under that role returns 'permission denied for table landing_cad_property'; information_schema.tables only lists objects a role holds some privilege on, which is why the RO enumeration didn't show the table -- it exists, the role just can't see it). doc-repo-26's enumeration and this lane's read were both correct for the role each used; there is no drift between the two handles.
reconciliationResolved.cortexStoreIdentity: cad_property lives in the store reached via PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL / STAGING_NEONDB_URL / CORTEX_DATABASE_URL -- confirmed these three secrets resolve to the same physical Neon endpoint (cortex-prod project, host ep-lucky-truth-apodo8hr, CORTEX_DATABASE_URL is the pooler variant of the same host PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL reaches directly). doc-repo-26's 'legacy-design-tools-prod' naming for this store was corrected in the same exchange; not a separate Neon project.
reconciliationResolved.provenanceVsContentRule: This lane's own attempted generalization (exclude any row whose source_file starts with 'stratmap25-landparcels') was WRONG and doc-repo-26 caught it by running the tie-breaker directly against cad_property's own land_value/land_acres/market_value columns. Verified finding: Williamson's 282,570 stratmap-sourced rows carry real land_value=0 and land_acres=0 for all of them (the genuine 'leftover farm' hollow-placeholder signature) -- but Bastrop's 62,257 stratmap-sourced rows are FULLY VALUED real accounts (land_acres populated on 62,257 of them, actually MORE completely than Bastrop's own 15,542-row real-export source, which only has land_acres on 1,598). For Bastrop the stratmap pass is a legitimate second source filling in accounts the county's own real export lacks, not a duplicate or a placeholder. Ruling: the gate must test CONTENT (does a cad_property row carry a real land_value or land_acres, regardless of which file it arrived in), never PROVENANCE (which source_file it came from) -- a provenance test is presence-shaped ('where did this come from') and infers realness from origin, which is exactly wrong for Bastrop.

correctedFigures.note: These are cad_property's own content-richness figures (how many of a county's cad_property rows carry a real land_value or land_acres), NOT yet a parcel_record-coverage figure -- see openQuestion below for why those are different questions.
correctedFigures.bastrop_48021: 77,799 of 77,799 real accounts (100% -- the stratmap rows are real too)
correctedFigures.williamson_48491: 319,480 of 602,050 real accounts (53.1% -- the 282,570 stratmap rows are the hollow placeholders; 271,164 of those DO carry a market_value despite zero land_value/land_acres, so they are not empty rows, they are specifically missing land valuation -- state it that precisely, not as a blanket 'placeholder')

openQuestionNotYetResolved.summary: The content-vs-provenance rule tells you how many of a county's cad_property rows are REAL accounts. It does not yet tell you how many of those real accounts have a corresponding parcel_record row, which is what this gate actually needs to measure (the gate's job is 'is parcel_record adequately instantiated for this county', not 'is cad_property itself well-formed'). This lane independently computed a THIRD number worth recording precisely because it is surprising and unverified beyond this session: a raw cross-store overlap of parcel_record's prop_id set against cad_property's full prop_id set (no content filter, all sources) gives Bastrop 62,256 of 77,799 = 80.0% -- meaning roughly 15,543 real Bastrop CAD accounts (per the content rule, ALL of Bastrop's cad_property rows are real) have NO parcel_record row at all, despite Bastrop being the most-published, most-mature CTX county in this sprint (25 bake executions). This number was verified free of the format-mismatch and source-exclusion bugs found earlier in this session (prop_id formats match exactly on both sides; a direct sample shows real, non-trivial divergence, e.g. cad_property has prop_id 10005 with no matching parcel_record row). This lane does NOT know whether an ~80% figure represents a genuine parcel-record-fill gap or a legitimate, by-design exclusion (e.g. exempt/right-of-way/government accounts that correctly never get a parcel_record) -- that requires domain knowledge of parcel-record-fill's own intended population, which is out of this lane's scope to determine unilaterally.
openQuestionNotYetResolved.recommendedNextBuild: requireCountyInstantiated should become a cross-store read: (1) query the TARGET store (via stores.DATABASE_URL, already resolved per-target by resolveTargetStores in runBastropPublish -- STAGING_NEONDB_URL or PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL) for the county's cad_property rows passing the content test (land_value IS NOT NULL AND land_value <> 0) OR (land_acres IS NOT NULL AND land_acres <> 0) -- this is the real denominator; (2) query the FACTORY store (already-connected factory.client) for parcel_record's distinct prop_id set for the county; (3) compute the real overlap (how many of the content-real cad_property prop_ids have a matching parcel_record row) EITHER via a single SQL query on the target store using `prop_id = ANY($parcelRecordPropIds::text[])` (avoids a large full-ID-set transfer in the other direction) OR via two ID-set fetches and a JS Set-intersection if that proves simpler -- both are cross-database reads since parcel_record and cad_property live in different databases with no FDW between them, so this cannot be a single joined SQL query. A generic connectByUrl(url, pgModule) helper (extracted from connect.mjs's connectFactory, same pooler-refusal and timeout discipline) is the natural building block for the cross-store connection -- prototyped and reverted this session, not committed, since the actual query shape wasn't settled at the time.
openQuestionNotYetResolved.beforeShipping: Before this new formula becomes a hard gate, someone who understands parcel-record-fill's intended population (which accounts are supposed to get a parcel_record vs. deliberately excluded) should confirm whether Bastrop's ~80% is a real gap or an expected exclusion rate -- shipping the corrected formula without that confirmation risks exactly what this lane avoided tonight: a readiness gate that starts refusing the program's own flagship 'done' county for a reason nobody can immediately explain.

action: No further code change made to src/lib/publish-readiness-gate.mjs or src/db/connect.mjs this session (a connectByUrl extraction was drafted and then reverted, since it had no consumer yet and the query shape it would serve is not settled). doc-repo-26 gave the same instruction three times across this exchange (do not rebuild without clear, settled ground) and this lane followed it each time, most concretely by reverting a partially-built change rather than shipping it once the Bastrop finding raised the stakes further than the Williamson-only picture had.
whatIsSettledAndNotOpen: The originally-merged gate (PR #100) still stands as shipped: its Williamson (46.9%) and Caldwell (51.4%) refusals and McLennan (99.999%) pass are unaffected by anything in this addendum -- both counties fail under every formula variant considered tonight (raw ratio, source-exclusion overlap, and the content-based figures above), so the gate's real-world behavior for the three counties it was built and verified against has not changed. What remains open is only whether the SAME gate, unmodified, would incorrectly flag other counties (Bastrop specifically, and by extension Hays/Travis, not checked this precisely this session) for the wrong reason if exercised -- which is exactly why this lane is recording it rather than either shipping a new formula or declaring the existing one sufficient.
